n: San Francisco de Asis Mission Church
w: Built between 1772 and 1816, this adobe church became the center of a small 18th-century Spanish and Native American farming community and has long been a favorite subject for painters. Declared a National Historic Landmark in 1970, it is a defining example of New Mexico Spanish Colonial church design.
s: An adobe church that became every artist's subject
_facts: Built 1772-1816 in Ranchos de Taos
Center of an 18th-century Spanish and Native American farming community
A popular subject for artists
Declared a National Historic Landmark in 1970

w: One of these 19th-century adobe houses belonged to Thomas 'Doc' Martin and hosted the 1915 meeting that founded the Taos Society of Artists. After his death, his widow Helen converted the houses into a hotel, opened June 7, 1936 as Hotel Martin, later renamed Taos Inn - added to the National Register in 1982.
s: Where the Taos Society of Artists was founded
_facts: Several 19th-century adobe houses, one home to Thomas 'Doc' Martin
Hosted the 1915 founding meeting of the Taos Society of Artists
Opened as Hotel Martin in 1936, later renamed Taos Inn
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982

w: New Mexico's second-oldest art museum, founded in 1923 by the Harwood Foundation and absorbed into the University of New Mexico in 1935. Its collection spans Hispanic works through the Taos Society of Artists and the Taos Moderns, in a campus that has since grown to include an auditorium and library.
_facts: Founded 1923 by the Harwood Foundation
Second-oldest art museum in New Mexico
Purchased by the University of New Mexico in 1935
Collections cover Hispanic works, the Taos Society of Artists and Taos Moderns

w: Hacienda de los Martinez was built during the Spanish colonial era on the bank of the Rio Pueblo de Taos and survives today as a living history museum. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, its adobe rooms preserve the setting of a frontier hacienda from New Mexico's years under Spanish rule.
s: A Spanish colonial hacienda turned living museum
_facts: Also known as Hacienda de los Martinez
Built during the Spanish colonial era
Located on the bank of the Rio Pueblo de Taos
Now a living museum, listed on the National Register of Historic Places

w: Russian emigre artist Nicolai Fechin bought this two-story adobe in 1927 and spent years reshaping it, carving doors, windows and furniture with Russian motifs layered over Spanish, Native American and Art Deco elements. His daughter Eya restored it in the 1970s, opening it in 1981; it now houses the Taos Art Museum.
s: A Russian artist's hand-carved adobe home
_facts: Bought and remodeled by Russian artist Nicolai Fechin from 1927
Fechin carved doors, windows and furniture with Russian design elements
Restored by daughter Eya Fechin, opened to visitors in 1981
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979; now the Taos Art Museum

w: Russian-born painter Leon Gaspard made this adobe house his home after joining the Taos art colony. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979, it has since passed into private hands and is no longer open to visitors - one more stop on the colony's scattered trail of artists' houses across town.
s: A private house from the Taos art colony's heyday
_facts: Home of Russian-born painter Leon Gaspard
Gaspard was a member of the Taos art colony
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979
Now a private residence, not open to the public

w: At 222 Ledoux Street stands the former home of Ernest L. Blumenschein (1874-1960), a co-founder of the Taos Society of Artists and one of the 'Taos Six' painters who put the town on the art map. Declared a National Historic Landmark in 1965, the adobe house now operates as a museum and gallery.
s: The Taos Six co-founder's adobe home and gallery
_facts: Home of painter Ernest L. Blumenschein (1874-1960)
Co-founder of the Taos Society of Artists, one of the 'Taos Six'
Located at 222 Ledoux Street, Taos
Declared a National Historic Landmark in 1965; now a house museum
